Description: SWE-bench Verified evaluates LLM-based software engineering agents on real GitHub issues by requiring them to produce patches that make repository tests pass, using a curated subset of tasks verified to be solvable. It emphasizes end-to-end bug fixing and feature implementation under realistic repo constraints and evaluation via automated test execution.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor), Language Production (minor)
L2: Planning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Adaptive Error Correction (minor)
L3:

Description: SWE-bench Multilingual extends SWE-bench-style repo-level issue resolution beyond Python to multiple programming languages and ecosystems, requiring agents to navigate varied build systems, idioms, and tooling. It measures cross-language transfer for debugging and patch generation under test-based verification.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor), Language Production (minor)
L2: Planning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory
L3: Cognitive Flexibility

Description: SWE-bench Pro is a larger, harder software engineering benchmark designed to be more challenging and more resistant to shortcuts, spanning multiple languages and more industrially realistic tasks. Models must generate correct patches within real repositories, typically validated by running project tests and checks.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Logical Reasoning, Decision-making, Working Memory
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: Terminal-Bench 2.0 evaluates agents operating in command-line environments on practical tasks such as installing dependencies, editing files, running programs, and diagnosing failures. Success requires choosing correct shell commands and iterating based on tool feedback under resource and time constraints.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor)
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory, Adaptive Error Correction
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: BrowseComp evaluates “deep research” behavior where models must locate, read, and synthesize information from the web (or a controlled web corpus) to answer difficult questions. It tests multi-step information seeking, source triage, and faithful synthesis rather than only recall.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor), Language Production (minor)
L2: Planning, Attention, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Working Memory
L3:

Description: τ2-bench measures an agent’s ability to handle multi-turn, policy-constrained customer-support style interactions while using tools and APIs to complete tasks. It emphasizes following domain rules, coordinating tool calls, and maintaining coherent dialogue across long interactions with a simulated user.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory
L3: Social Reasoning & Theory of Mind, Inhibitory Control, Empathy (minor)

Description: OSWorld is a multimodal “computer use” benchmark where agents must complete tasks in a desktop-like operating system environment using visual observations and UI interactions. It evaluates grounding in screenshots, navigation across apps, and reliable execution over multi-step workflows.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Visual Attention & Eye Movements, Planning, Decision-making, Sensorimotor Coordination (minor), Working Memory (minor)
L3:

Description: ARC-AGI-2 is a fluid-reasoning benchmark based on abstract grid transformations where models infer hidden rules from a few demonstrations and apply them to new inputs. It is designed to reduce reliance on memorized knowledge and emphasize generalization to novel patterns.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception (minor)
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Spatial Representation & Mapping
L3: Cognitive Flexibility

Description: Vending-Bench 2 evaluates long-horizon agent coherence by simulating operation of a vending-machine business over an extended period, requiring thousands of decisions about inventory, pricing, suppliers, and cash flow. The score reflects sustained strategy and adaptation rather than single-step correctness.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory, Reward Mechanisms
L3: Self-reflection (minor)

Description: MCP-Atlas evaluates real-world tool use via the Model Context Protocol (MCP), where agents must discover and correctly invoke tools across multi-step workflows and integrate results into correct final outputs. It stresses API selection, argument correctness, and robustness to tool errors in production-like settings.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: FinanceAgent assesses agent performance on tasks representative of entry-level financial analysts, such as interpreting financial statements, building analyses, and producing grounded written outputs. It rewards correct quantitative reasoning, structured reporting, and faithful use of provided data and tools where applicable.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Production (minor)
L2: Logical Reasoning, Planning, Working Memory, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Decision-making (minor)
L3:

Description: CyberGym evaluates cybersecurity agents on vulnerability identification and (in some settings) discovery in real open-source codebases, often starting from high-level weakness descriptions. It emphasizes code comprehension, hypothesis-driven investigation, and producing correct exploit/fix-related outputs under pass@1 scoring.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Planning, Attention, Working Memory, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: SpreadsheetBench measures an agent’s ability to understand and manipulate complex spreadsheets derived from realistic scenarios, including formula editing, data cleaning, and table restructuring. It rewards correct execution of multi-step transformations and maintaining consistency across interconnected cells and sheets.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Planning, Working Memory, Logical Reasoning, Attention (minor), Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: Humanity’s Last Exam (HLE) is a frontier, multimodal benchmark spanning many advanced domains where models must answer difficult questions and, in some variants, use tools like web search and code execution. It targets broad expert knowledge, robust reasoning, and the ability to synthesize across modalities and sources.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor), Visual Perception (minor)
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Planning (minor), Multisensory Integration (minor)

Description: AIME 2025 consists of competition-style math problems requiring multi-step symbolic reasoning and careful arithmetic, typically answered as integers. It evaluates correctness under limited context, with performance improving when models can maintain intermediate results and avoid algebraic slips.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: GPQA Diamond is a subset of very challenging graduate-level multiple-choice science questions designed to be difficult to solve via simple lookup. It tests deep scientific understanding and multi-step reasoning across physics, chemistry, and biology under tight answer selection constraints.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Logical Reasoning, Decision-making (minor), Working Memory (minor)
L3:

Description: MMMLU extends MMLU to many languages, evaluating broad academic knowledge and reasoning across subjects in multilingual settings. It tests whether models can transfer competence across languages without losing fidelity in meaning and domain terminology.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Logical Reasoning (minor), Working Memory (minor)
L3: Cognitive Flexibility (minor)

Description: MMMU is a multimodal benchmark requiring models to answer questions that combine images (diagrams, charts, screenshots, figures) with text across many disciplines. It probes whether models can ground language in visual evidence and perform cross-modal reasoning.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Multisensory Integration, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory (minor)
L3:

Description: MMMU-Pro is a more challenging variant/extension of MMMU intended to better stress expert-level multimodal reasoning, often with harder distractors and stronger requirements for grounded interpretation. It emphasizes robust visual understanding plus multi-step inference under professional-grade question design.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Multisensory Integration, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory (minor)
L3:

Description: LAB-Bench FigQA tests whether models can interpret scientific figures from biology papers and answer questions that require extracting evidence from plots, microscopy images, and complex multi-panel layouts. It targets figure-grounding, quantitative/causal interpretation, and avoiding unsupported claims.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Logical Reasoning, Attention (minor), Working Memory (minor)
L3:

Description: WebArena evaluates autonomous web agents performing realistic tasks across multiple websites (e-commerce, forums, CMS, Git, maps) using browser interaction. It stresses long-horizon navigation, form filling, search within sites, and recovery from UI and state changes under an automatic grader.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory, Visual Attention & Eye Movements, Sensorimotor Coordination (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: MathArena Apex is a set of difficult math problems (often beyond standard competition level) used to compare high-end mathematical reasoning, sometimes with or without tool assistance. It emphasizes sustained multi-step derivations, correctness under complex constraints, and robustness on hard distributions.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: 
L2: Logical Reasoning, Working Memory, Planning (minor)
L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: ScreenShot-Pro evaluates GUI understanding from high-resolution screenshots, requiring models to answer questions or take actions grounded in the visual interface. It emphasizes spatial grounding (where things are on screen), reading UI text, and understanding application state from visual cues.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Visual Perception
L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Visual Attention & Eye Movements, Spatial Representation & Mapping (minor), Working Memory (minor)

Cognitive Functions:

L2: Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning, Logical Reasoning, Working Memory (minor), Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition (minor)

L1: Visual Perception
L2: Multisensory Integration, Working Memory, Scene Understanding & Visual Reasoning
L3: Cognitive Timing & Predictive Modeling (minor)

Description: LiveCodeBench Pro evaluates coding ability on competitive-programming-like tasks and practical coding problems under controlled conditions, often reported with an ELO-style rating. It emphasizes producing correct executable solutions, reasoning about edge cases, and sometimes iterating with feedback depending on the harness.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Comprehension (minor), Language Production (minor)

L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

L1: Language Comprehension
L2: Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition, Logical Reasoning
L3: Cognitive Flexibility (minor)

Description: MRCR v2 (8-needle) tests long-context co-reference and retrieval by embedding multiple similar “needle” interactions in a large “haystack” and asking the model to reproduce the correct response tied to a specified needle. It measures whether models can maintain and correctly retrieve distributed information across long sequences without confusion.
Cognitive Functions:
L1:

L3: Inhibitory Control (minor)

Description: GDPval evaluates economically valuable knowledge work by having models produce real work artifacts (e.g., spreadsheets, slides, plans) across many occupations and judging outputs against expert professionals. It measures end-to-end project execution quality, including correctness, presentation, and adherence to a specification.
Cognitive Functions:
L1: Language Production
L2: Planning, Decision-making, Working Memory, Semantic Understanding & Context Recognition
L3: Self-reflection (minor)

Description: SWE-Lancer evaluates agentic software engineering in a setting that emphasizes autonomous completion of coding tasks with realistic constraints and strong verification. It targets robustness of code changes, tool usage, and the ability to ship working fixes rather than only proposing solutions.
Cognitive Functions:
